architecture_summary: Stakingverse runs a two-chain liquid staking protocol with completely different code on each chain. On Ethereum it operates a permissionless StakeWise V3 vault — the proxy is Stakingverse-deployed but delegates to StakeWise's audited EthVault implementation. On LUKSO it runs original Stakingverse-authored Solidity (StakingverseVault.sol derived from Universal.Page Vault.sol; SLYXToken.sol on LSP7 standard).

tvl_decomposition.method: DL adapter calls totalAssets() on each chain's proxy. Direct balance reflects un-staked float; remainder is staked into beacon-chain validators. v1 brief reported $88,912 on-chain TVL because it only read the Ethereum proxy's direct balance and never visited LUKSO.

v1_pipeline_errors.defect: LUKSO chain (chain_id 42) not recognized; all Stakingverse contracts placed on chain_id 1 (Ethereum)
v1_pipeline_errors.consequence: Contract 0x9f49a95b…f04 reported as 'unverified Ethereum contract' — actually the LUKSO StakingverseVaultProxy. SLYXToken (0x8A3982f0…7D), current StakingverseVault impl (0x1711b2e1…2D), legacy Vault impl, and current SLYXToken impl all entirely missed. ~5 of 7 production contracts not in v1 inventory.

v1_pipeline_errors.defect: Substring-matching on the project keyword harvested URLs from both github.com/stakewise/v3-core/audits/ AND github.com/Stakingverse/pool-contracts/audits/ without disambiguation. Both repos contain 'stake' in the path.
v1_pipeline_errors.consequence: 3 StakeWise V3 audit URLs (Halborn 2023-08, ConsenSys Diligence 2024-03, Sigma Prime 2024-09) attached to Stakingverse's docs_pages. Harvested as if they were Stakingverse's own audit history.

v1_pipeline_errors.defect: The single TP match — Halborn 2023-08 → EthVault — is technically a match against the correct bytecode (Halborn did audit StakeWise's EthVault) but is mislabeled as a Stakingverse audit when it belongs to StakeWise's audit programme.
v1_pipeline_errors.consequence: v1 reports '33.3% audit coverage' based on this misattribution. The true picture: Stakingverse's own audit programme (Extropy + MiloTruck + Enigma + Nethermind) is none of these matches; v1 missed all four of those audits entirely.

v1_pipeline_errors.defect: Reads the Ethereum proxy's direct ETH balance (~37.97 ETH ≈ $76K-$88K) instead of calling totalAssets() to capture validator-staked deposits.
v1_pipeline_errors.consequence: Reports '$88,912 on-chain TVL' against DL's $4.3M, flagging a phantom discrepancy. The real TVL is $4.6M with no missing accounting.

v1_pipeline_errors.defect: No 'operator-of-third-party-bytecode' attribution path. The pipeline cannot represent the StakeWise V3 vault operator pattern where Stakingverse runs but does not author the EthVault bytecode.
v1_pipeline_errors.consequence: EthVault reported as Stakingverse's own contract; StakeWise's audit programme attributed to Stakingverse. This same defect bites Swell (Nucleus boring vault) and stake.link (Chainlink OperatorStakingPool).

caveats: Multisig / timelock posture for the Stakingverse admin EOAs (0xe460f0cB on LUKSO, 0x93281072 on Ethereum) not inspected — both appear to be plain EOAs.
StakeWise vault admin role membership for the Ethereum proxy not extracted from EthVault storage.
Universal.Page upstream audit history not enumerated. Relevant only to the legacy 0x2Cb02ef…f4 Vault impl that is no longer in production.
LYX market price not separately verified — DL's implied $0.27/LYX is consistent with 2026 prices but not confirmed against deep liquidity.
Off-chain validator key custody and slashing posture (operated via github.com/Stakingverse/cli) is operational, not bytecode-related, and is out of audit scope here.
